transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate it. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but I've been having a little trouble keeping my words in a straight line lately. It's probably nothing too bad, maybe just stress, but... like, I'll start talking about an overnight shift at work—I'm an orderly—and then somehow I just end up jumping to soccer, or... or paint colors, or the patient charts. And I can just see everyone getting lost while I'm talking. It's really embarrassing, honestly. 

I hope that's the kind of thing I should be telling you? Does that make sense?
Do you have trouble keeping your words in a straight line all the time, or does it just happen sometimes?

Oh, um... well, I definitely try to make sure it's only sometimes. I don't want you to think I'm completely incapable or anything! I still work really hard, I promise. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it feels like it's happening a lot more lately. 

Like I mentioned before with the... the overnight shift and then suddenly talking about soccer or the charts. It's like I just lose the thread, and it slips out before I can stop it and fix it. I really try to catch myself when I see the other aides getting confused, but it's getting harder. 

I'm sorry if I'm just repeating myself, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Am I explaining it okay?
Are you having trouble doing your job as an orderly because of this issue with your words?

Oh, um... well, I really try not to let it affect the patients. I care about my job a lot, I really do! But... I guess, if I have to be completely honest... I have needed a little help lately. Just to be safe, you know? I've been having some of my coworkers double-check my rounds and my charting. I just don't want to make a mistake. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee... I'm really trying my best.

But, um... it's not just work, I guess. At home, I've sort of... fallen behind on my bills. And I've been ignoring my friends, which I feel awful about. My apartment has gotten completely out of control, too. I'm usually a much cleaner person, I promise! 

It actually... well, it got bad enough that employee health is the reason I'm here. They sent me for an emergency evaluation. I... I sort of admitted to them that I was thinking about suicide. I'm so sorry to just drop that on you, I know it's heavy, and I'm really ashamed to even say it out loud. I just want to be totally honest with you so I can get back to being a good orderly. Is... is it okay that I told you that?
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Um... well, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know a lot of people have it way worse than I do. But... yeah, I guess I have been feeling pretty sad lately. 

It's just... it's like this heavy, empty feeling, you know? And it's there most days, right from when I wake up. I try to put on a brave face for the patients and my coworkers, I really do! But... sometimes it's just so much. Like, after my shifts, I'll... I'll just sit in my car in the parking lot and cry for a while before I can even pull myself together enough to drive home. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so pathetic. I should be stronger than that. I really hope you don't think less of me for admitting it. Is it normal to feel that empty all the time?
Have you been experiencing a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Oh, um... well, I really try to stay active, I do! I don't want to just sit around all the time, that sounds so lazy. But... I guess lately, things I used to love just... don't feel the same. 

I used to do a lot, actually. I'd sketch murals, and I really loved cooking big meals for my friends. Oh, and I played soccer on the weekends, too! I promise I used to be really involved. But now... it all just feels sort of... pointless, I guess? Like I can't even find the energy to care about it anymore. 

Instead of going out, I've just been... ignoring my friends' messages and staying in my apartment. I know that makes me sound like such a bad friend, and I feel terrible about it, I really do. I just... I hope you don't think I'm just giving up. I want to enjoy those things again, I really do. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that right?
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns lately?

Oh, um... well, I really try to take good care of myself, I promise! I know how important it is to stay healthy, especially working around patients all day. But... I guess my appetite has been a little off lately. 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm starving myself on purpose or anything like that, I swear! It's just that I barely get hungry anymore. So a lot of days, I'll just drink coffee at work to try and keep my energy up, and maybe I'll eat some vending-machine crackers if I realize I haven't had anything all day. I am still having something, at least! 

But... I guess my clothes have gotten pretty loose lately. I've had to pull my work pants a lot tighter. I'm really sorry, I know I should be eating real meals and taking better care of my body. I'm going to try to force myself to eat more, I really will. I hope you don't think I'm being totally irresponsible with my health... is it normal to just lose your appetite like that?
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide besides what you mentioned earlier?

Um... well, I really don't want to alarm you, and I promise I'm not trying to be dramatic or anything. I know you deal with people who have much bigger problems than I do... 

But, um... yeah, I guess I have had some thoughts like that. It's just... after those really bad nights, you know, when I can't sleep and everything feels so heavy... I just keep thinking that it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up the next morning. 

And... sometimes, I'm really sorry to even admit this, but sometimes the thought comes into my head that I should just... end it. But I swear, I don't want you to think I'm actually going to do it! Whenever it happens, I get really scared, and I always make sure to tell someone about it. I really try to handle it the right way, I promise. I just... I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or like a burden. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, empty feeling?

Um... well, I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just complaining, because I know I should be stronger than this. I really do try to push through it and put on a brave face at work, I promise! 

But... I guess this heavy feeling, and the... not caring about things I used to like... it's been going on for a while now. Maybe... about a year and two months? Give or take? 

I know that sounds like a really long time to just let myself feel this way, and I'm so sorry I haven't been able to snap out of it on my own. I really thought I could just work hard and get past it, you know? I didn't want to bother anyone with it until I absolutely had to. I hope you don't think I'm just wallowing in it or being weak for letting it go on this long. Am I making sense? Is that the kind of answer you needed?
Have you been feeling restless or sluggish lately?

Um... well, I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy. I promise I always try to keep up with my duties at the hospital, I know the nurses rely on me. But... um... I guess people have been making comments lately. They tell me I look like I'm moving like I'm underwater. I really don't mean to be slow, I swear, it's just like my body won't cooperate sometimes and everything takes so much effort. 

But then, it's weird, because other times it's the exact opposite. I don't want you to think I'm acting strange or anything, but... I get so wound up I can't even sit down. I'll just keep pacing back and forth in my apartment for a really long time, or I'll catch myself rubbing my hands together over and over until they're completely sore. 

I try really hard to hide it when I'm around other people, I promise. I don't want to make anyone uncomfortable or look like I'm out of control. Is... is that what you meant by restless and sluggish? I hope I'm explaining it okay for you.
Have you noticed any changes in how fast or slow you move or react to things?

Oh, um... I'm so sorry, I think that's kind of what I was just trying to explain a second ago. Did I... did I not answer it right the first time? I'm really sorry if I was rambling and didn't make sense, I can definitely try to explain it better! 

But, yeah, it's just like I was saying. The nurses at the hospital, they'll tell me I'm reacting to things way too slow, like I'm stuck underwater. I swear I'm trying my absolute hardest to move fast when they need me to help with a patient, but my body just feels like lead sometimes. 

And then the fast part is when I get all worked up and can't sit still, like when I'm pacing holes in the floor of my apartment or rubbing my hands together until they're completely raw and sore. I really do try to keep that under control so nobody sees me acting weird. 

I hope it's okay that I repeated myself... I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need. Did I do a better job answering it this time?
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous lately?

Um... actually, no, I don't think so. I really hope it's okay to say that! I know I just told you about the pacing and being all wound up, so I don't want you to think I'm contradicting myself or trying to hide being nervous from you. I promise I'd tell you if I was! 

But... I don't really feel worried or scared about things, you know? It's more just that heavy, empty feeling I mentioned, or my body just feeling restless on its own. I don't really have that... that nervous, panicky feeling in my mind. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I'm so sorry if that messes up your notes or if I'm supposed to be feeling that way. I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest and giving you the right information. Is it alright that I don't have that one?
Have you had any periods in the last two weeks where you felt significantly better, even if only for a few days?

Um... no, not really. I'm sorry, I really wish I could say yes, because I know you want me to be getting better. I really do try to feel better, I promise! I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it or not trying hard enough. 

But... um... it's just been pretty much the same. Just that heavy, low feeling the whole time. I haven't really had any good days lately. 

I'm really sorry if that's disappointing to hear. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me. I promise I'll keep trying to have a good day, though!
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Um... I mean, I try to. I really do! I know I'm supposed to be keeping busy and doing things that are good for me. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or being lazy. 

But... well, I used to do a lot of stuff. I used to sketch these big murals, and I'd cook dinner for my friends, and we'd play soccer on the weekends. I was always doing something. But lately... um... it all just feels kind of pointless, I guess? 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds terrible and like I'm not trying. But I just... I usually just end up ignoring my friends' messages and staying in my apartment. I really hope you aren't mad at me for that. I know I should be doing those things, and I promise I'll try harder to go out and play soccer or something if you think I should. Is it okay that I haven't been doing them lately?
Have you had any periods in the last two months where you felt significantly better for at least two weeks?

Um... well, there was a little bit of time. I really hope I'm remembering this right, I want to give you the exact right timeline. But, um, maybe about a month ago? There was a stretch for a few weeks where I wasn't feeling quite so heavy and down. I actually felt... okay, mood-wise, I think. 

I don't want to mislead you, though! I wasn't completely better. I'm sorry, I know you probably want to hear that everything was totally fine then. But... even though I wasn't in that deep, dark place, I was still... well, I still knew about the cameras. And the supervisors monitoring me. So I was still having to be really careful and guarded at work during those weeks. 

I'm sorry, does that count as feeling significantly better? I hope it's okay that I still had the camera stuff going on even when my mood lifted. I promise I was trying my best to just do my job as an aide and act normal for them! Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Do you think your feelings of sadness and emptiness are mild, moderate, or severe?

Um... I guess... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much, I know so many people have it worse. And I really do try to keep a brave face, especially at work. I don't want to be a burden to anyone. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... I think it's pretty severe. Most days, I just feel this... this heaviness and emptiness right from the time I wake up. And, um, it gets really hard after my shifts at the hospital. I'll actually just sit in my car crying for a while before I can even pull myself together enough to drive home. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds really pathetic. I promise I'm trying to handle it better! I don't want you to think I'm just letting it completely take over. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not overreacting by calling it severe.
How long have you been feeling this way without any significant improvement?

Um... well, it's been a while, I guess. I really hope I haven't let it go on for too long without getting help, I know I probably should have come in sooner. I'm sorry if I waited too long. 

But, um, I think this heaviness... the depression and just not caring about things anymore... it's been with me for about a year and two months now? I mean, I've really tried to push through it and just keep working and being normal, I promise I have! I haven't just been sitting around the whole time. But yeah, it's been about fourteen months since I really felt like myself. Is that... is that a really long time to feel like this? I hope you're not disappointed that I let it go on for so long.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but no longer find pleasure in?

Um... well, I really try to stay busy, I promise. I don't want to sound like I just do nothing. But... yeah, there are a few things. 

I used to really love sketching murals, and I'd cook for my friends a lot. We used to play soccer on the weekends, too. But lately... um, for a while now, actually... it all just feels kind of pointless? I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible. I really should make more of an effort with my friends. But I usually just end up ignoring their messages and staying in my apartment. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend or a lazy person. I really do want to enjoy those things again, I just... I can't seem to find the energy for it right now. Is it normal to lose interest like that? I'm trying to get better, I really am.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling severely empty and heavy, is it constant or are there moments where it feels slightly better?

Um... well, it's pretty much all the time. I really don't want to sound dramatic, and I know I already mentioned this, so I'm sorry to repeat myself... but it really is most days. I just wake up and there's this... this awful heaviness, like I'm totally empty inside. 

I try really hard to shake it off, I promise I do. I smile at the patients and the nurses at the hospital, and I do my job. But... um, it doesn't really go away. And then, like I said, after my shift... I just can't hold it in anymore. I'll just sit in my car in the parking lot and cry for a while. I have to do that before I can even pull myself together enough to drive back to my apartment. 

I'm really sorry, I know that probably sounds so weak, and I really should be able to handle my emotions better. I don't want you to think I'm not trying. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm not doing something wrong by letting it get to me like that.
You mentioned earlier that you've been feeling severely empty and heavy, can you tell me if there are any times when this feeling is not as severe?

Um... well, there was a time, actually. I really hope I'm explaining this right, and I'm sorry if it's confusing. But... um, maybe a little while back, there was a stretch of a few weeks where that really awful, heavy feeling kind of lifted? Like, I wasn't in that deep, dark place where I couldn't stop crying. I felt a little more normal, I guess. 

But... um... I don't know if this is what you're asking for, and I feel really silly even saying it out loud. Even though I wasn't feeling as sad, I still... I still felt like I had to be really careful at work. I still thought the cameras were watching me, and that my supervisors were monitoring everything I did. So I kept acting really guarded around them. 

I know that probably sounds strange, and I'm sorry if it's not the right kind of answer. I just wanted to be honest that even when the sadness wasn't as bad, that other stuff was still happening. Is it okay that I still felt that way even when I wasn't as depressed? I hope I'm making sense.
Have you experienced any hallucinations or delusions recently?

Um... well, I don't know if I'd call them delusions, really. I mean, I try to be very rational about things, I promise. But... um... I guess there are some things that feel very real to me, even if others say they aren't? I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or anything.

Like at work... um, my shifts keep getting changed around. And I know, I know people say it's just because of staffing shortages, and I really try to believe them. I don't want to be a difficult employee. But... I'm just so sure that the supervisors are doing it on purpose. Like they're watching me through the unit cameras to see if I'm... if I'm unsafe or doing something wrong. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really paranoid, and I really don't want you to think badly of me. I just... I can't shake the feeling that they're monitoring me, even when I try to tell myself it's just regular hospital stuff. Is it normal to feel that way when you're under a lot of stress? I'm really trying my best to just do my job and not cause any trouble.
